shared_elements: tall upright stone slab/monolith with carved surface
shallow low-relief carving in pale tan stone
profile head facing left in the upper zone
horizontal band of repeating pattern across the upper part
serpentine/curvilinear zoomorphic motifs near the base
weathered, chipped edges of a single stone block
justification: Both are tall pale limestone blocks bearing shallow relief with a horizontal patterned band in the upper zone and a leftward-facing profile head beneath it, which gives a broadly similar first impression. But A is a single dense, bilaterally symmetrical anthropomorphic figure built from tightly packed rectilinear, glyph-like ornament filling the whole field, whereas B scatters a few isolated, rounded, naturalistic animal forms across a mostly empty surface — the compositional logic and the carving idiom are quite different.
